provenance: Opus 5.5 subscription CLI draft with host review/repairs, source restrictions and execution verification.

draft_notes.explanation: The background is palette[0] and the hollow frame is palette[1]. The program finds the frame's bounding box from the visible frame-coloured cells, so its interior is located without any rotation. The seed diagonal starts at the original top-left grid corner. The factory tracks where that corner lands in the visible grid: reversing each row flips the left/right flag, and each clockwise turn maps (top, left) to (left, not top). The seeds are all remaining non-background, non-frame cells outside the interior. They are ordered by their Chebyshev distance from that visible corner, which reproduces the original order (0,0), (1,1), .... Each interior cell gets depth = min(distance to the four interior edges). It is coloured seeds[min(depth, n-1)], so the last seed colour keeps filling inward when there are more rings than seeds. Ring depth is symmetric under D4, so the fill needs no direction-specific change beyond the seed ordering. This matches the generator's hollow_rect loop, which shrinks the rectangle by 2 per ring until a dimension reaches 0 or below. The rule is consistent with all supplied fixtures.
draft_notes.limitations: It assumes seed colours are never the background colour (original 0); a 0 seed would be invisible yet still used by the generator. Whether common.random_colors excludes 0 needs host review; the archived solver has the same blind spot. It assumes common.hollow_rect fills a 1-wide or 1-tall rectangle as a solid line, so the core is fully painted (as in the fixture's 1x2 core). The frame is assumed to be the only object in colour palette[1], since the constructor excludes 1 from the seed colours. Not executed or tested by me.
draft_notes.host_review: Inspected common.random_colors: samples from 1..9, never background 0. The conditional background-ambiguity concern is resolved.
